$comment: Session boundary for the bridge (plan.md 6.2). What enforces the boundary is the commit gate, checks 35 and 41; this file states it, and only part of it is enforced at write time. Read the three comments in permissions before trusting any single line: the entries are in three groups and they do not all do the same amount.

permissions.$comment_1_reachable: THE FIRST EIGHT ENFORCE. A path pattern resolves against the session's root, which for this seat is bridge/, so a pattern naming something inside bridge/ does resolve: Write(tasks/**) means bridge/tasks/**. All four are manager-owned (seats.json, manager-bridge) and all four are reachable from an execution session, which until 2026-09-19 left the descending instructions, the standing orders and this file itself writable by the seat they constrain. tasks/ is the home of what comes down (6.2-2); a seat that can edit its own instructions has none. This is the shape architecture ruled for the execution agents, where the two reachable paths are envelope/safety.json and inbox/**; the bridge has neither, and its manager-owned files are the equivalent. Not a constraint on the manager seat: manager sessions sit at the repository root (D12), so this file is not theirs to load. threads/ and failures.jsonl are this seat's own and are not denied.
permissions.$comment_2_command: THE COMMAND PATTERN ENFORCES, and for a different reason: a command is not a path and has no root to resolve against. Tool denies are the part of this file that has worked all along -- the bridge having no instrument tools is enforced today. Do not read the group below and conclude the file is decorative.
permissions.$comment_3_outward: THE REST ARE INERT, and wrong if they ever resolve. Write(microscope_agent/**) from this root means bridge/microscope_agent/**, a path that cannot exist, and every entry naming a sibling, contracts/ or plan.md is the same. That is the defect class section 7 documents for .mcp.json -- the interpretation point must not be the session's cwd -- but here there is no portable way to say it: a permission pattern is a literal, so there is no $(git rev-parse), and an absolute path is the answer section 7 already rejected because it is the same string in every worktree. Kept because they are correct for a session rooted at the repository root and because deleting them would delete the statement of intent. If a bridge session is ever rooted there, remove <agent>/inbox/ from these first: as written they would block the delivery 7.1 rule 8 requires of this seat.

hooks.$comment: The validator's exit code is the only truth (plan.md 8). Resolved from the git root rather than from $CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR, which is the session's cwd: rooted at bridge/ it looked for bridge/contracts/validate.py and failed on every write in every bridge session, silently, because a PostToolUse failure does not stop the write. Same resolution .mcp.json uses, and for the same reason.
